pairs.question: Quod, virgo, tibi nomenque genusque, quae sors ista, doce, tendunt cur vincula palmas?
pairs.answer: Nos Ili felix quondam genus, invida donec Laomedonteos fugeret fortuna penates.
pairs.derivation: Hercules (ductor ait) asks the chained virgin Hesione her name, lineage (genus), fate (sors), and why she is bound; question taken verbatim, dropping the speech tag 'ductor ait'. Her reply opens with the non-answering deflection 'non ego digna malis. suprema parentum / dona vides ostro scopulos auroque frequentes.' which laments rather than answers; the answer window advances to the operative sentence stating her lineage ('nos Ili felix quondam genus... penates'), which answers the genus/origin question. Cut stops at 'penates.' (first full stop of the answering sentence); what follows ('principio morbi...') digresses into the plague and sea-monster narrative.
